My first job had a filing cabinet with a lock that didn't lock. Everyone knew. Nobody fixed it, because the cabinet was "secure" on the asset register, and that was what counted.

I think about that cabinet a lot. It's the perfect picture of security that looks fine on paper and fails the moment you touch it.

Last month a colleague asked me how we'd know if our new tools were leaking anything. Honest answer? We wouldn't, not quickly. We had a register, a policy and a training video. We didn't have a way to see what actually left the building.

So we started small. One team, one week, a spreadsheet and a lot of awkward conversations. It wasn't pretty, and I got some things badly wrong (sorry, finance), but by Friday we knew more than the register had told us in a year.

That's my advice, for what it's worth. Before you buy the shiny thing, go and rattle the cabinet. You'll learn more in an afternoon than in a quarter of reports.
